description: owine/* baseline — supply-chain hardened defaults. Pin everything, soak releases, escalate CVEs.

schedule: on monday, wednesday, friday and sunday

packageRules.description: Reclaim `deps:` as the baseline commit type. The top-level `semanticCommitType: deps` above is INERT on its own: Renovate ships two built-in default packageRules — `{matchPackageNames:['*'] => chore}` and `{matchDepTypes:['dependencies','require'] => fix}` — and packageRules ALWAYS beat top-level config, so without this override every bump commits as `chore:` (npm prod deps as `fix:`). That matters because release-please treats `chore:` as a HIDDEN, non-releasing type: Dockerfile/Actions/apk repos would cut zero releases and add nothing to the changelog. This catch-all re-forces `deps:` for every package (release-please recognizes `deps` as a releasable unit => patch, in a dedicated Dependencies changelog section). Ordered FIRST so the more specific rules below/after still win where they match: lock file maintenance => chore, CI/Actions => ci, security => fix (vulnerabilityAlerts, force). Nothing in this fleet types a dependency update `feat:` — majors included; see the major rule below.

Lock file maintenance commits as `chore:` — the ONE update type that must NOT cut a release. It refreshes transitive/nested deps within existing manifest ranges (no direct-dependency change consumers can see) and runs 4x/week (mon/wed/fri/sun, see the lockFileMaintenance block). Under the `deps:` baseline above it is a release-please releasable unit => a patch release every refresh = pure changelog/version spam. `chore:` is release-please's HIDDEN, non-releasing type, so refreshes stay silent. Uses matchUpdateTypes:['lockFileMaintenance'] (not matchPackageNames) because the maintenance branch has no depName; ordered AFTER the catch-all so it wins over `* => deps`.

Major bumps — separate PR per package, 7-day soak, manual review required. Deliberately sets NO semanticCommitType: it falls through to the `* => deps` catch-all above and cuts a PATCH release, in the changelog's Dependencies section alongside routine churn. This rule used to type majors `feat:` (minor release, Features section); that is gone, because `feat:` should mean a feature someone here wrote, not an upstream version number crossing a line — inflating consumers' minor versions on dependency churn made the minor digit meaningless. Nothing Renovate generates is `feat:` any more. What still marks a major as special is the review surface, not the commit type: its own branch (separateMajorMinor/separateMultipleMajor), a 7-day soak, automerge off, and the `major-update`/`needs-review` labels. Also still not `feat!:`/breaking: an upstream major is not automatically the consumer's breaking change.

Pins run OFF-SCHEDULE, overriding the top-level `schedule: on monday`. `pin` and `pinDigest` are the only update types that change neither the resolved version nor the resolved artifact — they change only how it is written down: `pin` rewrites a range to the exact version already resolving under it (rangeStrategy is `pin` fleet-wide), and `pinDigest` appends the digest the tag already points at. There is nothing to soak and nothing to review, so holding them for up to six days leaves a newly-added dependency floating for most of a week in a preset whose whole premise is that nothing floats. `digest` is DELIBERATELY NOT HERE — a digest REFRESH re-points an unchanged tag at different bytes, which is a content change and belongs in the reviewed weekly bundle; only the tag->digest CONVERSION is a pin. THIS RULE IS HALF THE CHANGE: a groupName is a branch name and a branch gets ONE schedule, so this override is inert on its own for any consumer extending automerge.json, whose `all non-major dependencies` bundle used to sweep pin/pinDigest onto the weekly branch. That preset now carves them onto their own `pins` branch; keep the two matchUpdateTypes lists in sync or pins silently revert to Monday. Same mechanism alpine.json documents for its off-schedule apk group. `minimumReleaseAge` is left at the 3-day baseline on purpose rather than zeroed: it is a near-no-op here (the version being pinned already satisfies the existing range, so it is long since released), and zeroing it would be a soak-policy change wearing a scheduling change's clothes. KNOWN, ACCEPTED GAP: the ecosystem groups in node.json/python.json and the `github-actions-*` groups in docker.json carry NO matchUpdateTypes, so they match every update type including pin/pinDigest and, being extended later, win the groupName over automerge.json's `pins`. A pin swept into one of those branches still runs at any time whenever it is the branch's ONLY pending upgrade (the branch then has nothing but anytime upgrades on it); it reverts to Monday only when a version bump in the same group is pending in the same run. Deliberately NOT fixed by bolting a negation onto ~55 grouping rules: that would put a scheduling concern into every ecosystem rule in the fleet and rot on the next group added. docker.json's `dockerfile bases` IS fixed, because it named `pinDigest` explicitly and pinDigest is the one conversion that recurs — every new FROM line produces one.

CI plumbing commits as `ci:` — release-please's HIDDEN, non-releasing type. Actions, reusable workflows and composite `action.yml` files are build-time infrastructure: nothing a consumer of the published image/package/server can observe, so bumping actions/checkout should neither cut a patch release nor add a changelog line. Ordered AFTER the `* => deps` catch-all and the major rule so it wins for every update type, major included — a GHA major still gets that rule's 7-day soak, `automerge: false` and `major-update`/`needs-review` labels, it just doesn't release. Security is exempt automatically: `vulnerabilityAlerts.semanticCommitType: fix` is applied at force level and beats every packageRule, so a CVE in an action still lands in Bug Fixes and cuts a release. Covers `.github/workflows`, `.github/actions`, `workflow-templates/` and any `action.yml` — the github-actions manager's own file patterns.

Same `ci:` treatment for the workflow version literals the customManagers block below extracts — annotated tool versions in matrix arrays, run-step args and env defaults, AND the non-literal runner labels (`matrix.include[].runner`, `workflow_call` input defaults, JSON-in-`run:`) picked up by the second manager — all inside `.github/workflows/*.yml`. Those deps belong to the custom regex manager, not `github-actions`, so the matchManagers rule above can't reach them; they are matched by path instead. This is what keeps a runner-label bump typed `ci:` and consistent with the literal `runs-on:` half of the very same PR. Deliberately NOT `matchManagers: ['custom.regex']`, which would also silence any unrelated custom manager a consumer repo defines.
Pin Docker image and GitHub Action digests so a re-tagged image/action can't slip in

NEVER pin a digest onto a `uses-with` dep — it is physically impossible and hard-errors the branch. The github-actions manager extracts THREE deps from one annotated action step: the `uses:` line (depType `action`, digest belongs there), the action's `version:` INPUT for actions it knows how to read (depType `uses-with`, datasource github-releases), and — where the repo also carries a `# renovate:` comment — a third dep from this file's customManagers. The rule above matches `matchManagers: [github-actions]`, i.e. the WHOLE manager, so it switched pinDigests on for the `uses-with` dep too. A `with: version: '0.16.7'` input has nowhere to put a 40-char SHA: auto-replace rewrites the value, then asserts the result contains newDigest, fails that assert, and returns a branch-level `Error updating branch: update failure` with the upgrade listed under Errored on the Dependency Dashboard. Observed on owine/claude-terminal-home-assistant `.github/workflows/lint.yml` (astral-sh/ruff-action + `version: '0.16.7'`), run 2026-09-21: branch `renovate/pins`, `ci: pin dependency ruff to b5dba86`, result `error`. PRE-DATES the off-schedule `pins` split and was not caused by it — pinDigests generates this upgrade regardless of which branch it lands on. The split only made it VISIBLE: the impossible upgrade used to be one of 14 on the weekly bundle, and is now alone on a branch that therefore cannot do anything but fail, every run, because pins are unscheduled. Upstream gets this right — `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests`, which this preset already extends, scopes itself to `matchDepTypes: [action]` rather than to the manager. DELIBERATELY a negation rather than narrowing the rule above to `matchManagers: [dockerfile]`: workflow `container:`/`services:` images (depTypes `container`/`service`) are real Docker refs that SHOULD stay digest-pinned, and dropping github-actions from that rule would silently unpin them.
docker-compose: bump tags but never pin digests — keeps compose files readable for humans editing them by hand

Node version pins use LTS-aware versioning — Renovate's 'node' versioning scheme tracks LTS lines (22, 24, 26, ...) and skips Current/odd-numbered releases (23, 25, 27, ...). LTS-to-LTS major bumps still come as separate manual-review PRs via the major-bump rule above.

customManagers.description: Make runner labels visible where they are NOT a literal `runs-on:` value. Renovate's github-actions manager extracts runners from literal `runs-on:` ONLY (its docs say so outright for env vars), so a label reached indirectly is invisible — and merging Renovate's partial PR then ships a SPLIT-BRAIN build (some jobs on the new image, some on the old) that stays GREEN, because both images work. Three shapes are covered, all observed in owine/*: (a) `matrix.include[]` entries `runner: ubuntu-26.04` — doc-scanner, youth-activity-scheduler, nut-cgi, MLB-Deferred-Contract-Calculator, house-manager; (b) a reusable-workflow `workflow_call` input named `runner` whose `default:` carries the label — compose-workflow, which today has 3 such defaults alongside 4 literal `runs-on:` and is one Renovate PR away from split-brain; (c) the same key inside a JSON string in a `run:` step, `"runner":"ubuntu-26.04"` — trip-tracker's dynamically-built matrix. INVARIANT — the capture must mirror the built-in manager's own regex `^\s*(?<depName>[a-zA-Z]+)-(?<currentValue>[^\s]+)`: `currentValue` takes the WHOLE remainder, suffix included, because the github-runners datasource carries `26.04-arm`, `15-large` and `15-intel` as distinct versions — `24.04-arm` is NOT `24.04` with decoration. Capturing a bare `\d+\.\d+` would file the arm runner under the x64 runner's version and could propose a label that does not exist for arm. Matching the built-in extraction byte-for-byte also makes these deps collapse into the SAME branch as the literal `runs-on:` ones, which is what turns two half-PRs into one whole one. No `autoReplaceStringTemplate` on purpose: the default value-only replacement rewrites exactly the `currentValue` span. No `versioningTemplate` either — the github-runners datasource defaults to `docker` versioning, same as the built-in manager. INVARIANT — inter-field separators use `[ \t]`, never `\s`, so a match cannot leak across lines (see PR #4); `\s` appears only inside negated classes as a value terminator, which is the opposite concern. The multi-line pattern (b) is bounded to <=6 intervening lines that each carry a `key: value` pair, so it stops at the next bare block-opening key and cannot latch onto a sibling input's `default:`; it also cannot match the `description:` line that quotes a sample label, because `default:` is required immediately before the value. These deps belong to `custom.regex`, not `github-actions`, so they are typed `ci:` by the `matchFileNames: ['.github/workflows/**']` rule above, not by the `matchManagers` one.
